scope: Independent final assurance and 2026-11-10 live re-verification of the canonical root and hub edition. No personal identifiers; no attorney review; no private-record inference.

corrections.finding: The hard gate is a current license on the increase's effective date. Completing Housing Inventory reporting before serving notice is the safer workflow, not a universal claim that notice itself is the statutory cutoff. Late reporting is prospective; ordinary annual/banked notices are not filed for Board approval.
The brief supplies $3,150.00 only as the June 1, 2019 lease-start rent. All Unit 2 outputs are now labeled illustrations on that input; the official current-base confirmation is blank.

Unit 1's April 1, 2026 instrument was not supplied. If it created an unmodified fixed term through March 31, 2027, the February 1 scenario is unavailable. A later effective date requires the unpublished future rate.

The 24-month guidance measures the no-increase period; Rule 4.12 measures 12 months from when the skipped allowance became available. February 1, 2027 satisfies both for the Unit 1 scenario. The actual ledger still controls availability.

Section 37.3(b)(5), Rule 4.10(b), and Rule 4.12(b) must be stated together. In particular, Rule 4.12(b) expressly says omission of banked dates does not itself render an increase null and void. Full itemisation remains the conservative practice.

Civil Code §1942.5 is not an automatic 180-day moratorium on every increase. Protected activity, statutory conditions, lawful cause, and any asserted good-faith ground require review. Repair petitions are a separate risk.

The Rent Board says no lawyer is needed to petition and publishes referral resources. It does not guarantee every tenant free representation for notice review; provider eligibility, scope, capacity, and cost must be checked.

Raising one unit is not automatically discrimination, and identical treatment is not immunity. Protected-class selection, retaliation, bad-faith conduct, and independent defects in either increase remain relevant.

The DOJ RealPage announcement is used only as an enforcement example with allegations and a proposed settlement. It is not evidence that all corporate landlords behave alike. San Francisco's covered algorithm ban applies to individuals and corporations.
The Rent Board's current rent-increase and banking pages contain inconsistent worked-example year labels. Form 571 supplies the rate periods used here; erroneous example labels were not copied.

corrections.item: Rent Board Fee separated from license and base rent
corrections.finding: The 2026–27 dwelling-unit fee is $59.00 unless exempt. After full payment, 50% may be recoverable only from tenants in occupancy on the applicable November 1; penalties are not recoverable. It is separate from the free license and scenario base-rent arithmetic.

corrections.item: Reasonableness and owner-behavior values remain blank
corrections.finding: No official ZIP-specific normal market increase or SF behavior-by-owner-type dataset was located. The 1.6% annual allowance is a routine planning scenario, not an official market average or guarantee of acceptance.

corrections.item: 2026-11-10 live verification, File #261020 retroactive trigger, §13.14 & 2027 deadlines, and template/count fixes
corrections.finding: Re-fetched all 29 prior official sources plus 5 additional official .gov sources (Rules Part XIII §13.14, 2027 Fee/Inventory Notice, 42 U.S.C. §3604 on U.S. GPO, Noncompliance Notice, and 2024 Census/HUD RHFS CB26-TPS.12). Added the November 9, 2026 Rent Board warning and draft File #261020 text applying the 10%/yr cap retroactively to banked notices provided on or after September 15, 2026 (through Dec 31, 2029), plus the December 14, 2026 2027 fee-exemption cutoff. Fixed unformatted literal placeholders in index.html, stale counts/dates in hub/review.html, hub/flags.html, hub/sources.html, assurance/index.html, and README.md, and trailing-dot Civil Code §1942.5 links.
